title: tier-2 shipped code: the hex-pair decoder against HexPairDecode (0x14269ab80)

unreachableBranches.why: null text pointer (`test r8, r8; je`): arena pointers are never null, and a len of 0 covers the sibling guard at 0x14269aba1. The probe cannot construct a null pointer, so this edge cannot run in the oracle.

high-nibble value conversion fall-through to `xor ecx, ecx`: to reach it a character must pass the byte-range validation at 0x14269abe9..0x14269ac02 (exactly 0-9/a-f/A-F, as an al/dl byte test) yet fail all three 32-bit value tests at 0x14269ac29..0x14269ac44. No byte does: each byte range that passes validation is exactly one of those three value ranges, so a validated character is always a digit, a-f, or A-F and the xor edge is dead.

low-nibble value conversion fall-through to `xor eax, eax`: the same argument for the second character - validation at 0x14269ac08..0x14269ac27 admits exactly 0-9/a-f/A-F, which are exactly the three value ranges tested at 0x14269ac4d..0x14269ac6c, so a validated character never reaches the xor.

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/install.rs::hex_decode (with its hex_value leaf, used by parse_hex_key and parse_hex_key_id), built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the hex_pair_decode entry. The ledger binds the verdict to install.rs + the probe source + the git revision. The shipped helper matched the client operation for operation and needed no signature change: it already took (out, count, text-slice) where the slice length is the client's len, returned the bytes written, never zeroes out, and stops at need-a-pair, NUL (as a non-hex first character), a non-hex character, or count.

Oracle is HexPairDecode at exe 0x14269ab80, measured extent 0x14269ab80..0x14269acbe (318 bytes through the ret at 0x14269acbd), which is the declared coverageWindow. The .pdata extent is only 0x36 bytes (0x14269ab80..0x14269abb6); the rest is the chained body the merged project and rd.py read - the fn_extent root stops at the pdata seam. The next code at 0x14269acc0 is a separate thunk that jumps to 0x14269ab80 with r9 = -1. Signature: (u8 *out, u64 count, const char *text, u64 len) -> u64 written (RCX, RDX, R8, R9; the return is (cursor - text) >> 1 after a cqo, i.e. the bytes written).

The client's read: `test r8, r8; je` and `test r9, r9; je` return 0; `test rdx, rdx; je` (count 0) skips the loop and returns 0. Per pair: `offset >= len - 1` (jae, offset = cursor - text) ends the run, so an odd trailing character is never read; the first character is sign-extended (movsx) and a NUL ends the run; both characters pass three range tests in order - `cmp edx, 0x30` / `cmp dl, 0x39` for 0-9, `lea eax, [rdx - 0x61]; cmp al, 5` for a-f (a byte test on al), `sub dl, 0x41; cmp dl, 5` for A-F (a byte test on dl) - so high-bit bytes are rejected by the byte tests, not by the sign extension. Value conversion is 32-bit: a digit keeps its ASCII in ecx and `shl cl, 4` keeps only the low nibble (the digit), a-f subtracts 0x57, A-F subtracts 0x37, and the low nibble is the analogous eax value added to the shifted high byte; both are exactly (high << 4) + low in a byte, as the shipped helper writes. The loopback is `cmp r11, rbx; jb` (written < count, unsigned).

Compared channels: the 64-bit return (bytes written), the 32-byte out block and the read-only text. The fixture pre-fills out with 0xA5 sentinels, so the client's no-zeroing contract (only written bytes change), the partial writes before a stop, and the count stop are all compared; a decoded 0xa5 byte is also present so a sentinel value cannot hide a missing write.

Coverage gate is 100% over the window's sites: the len-0 and count-0 exits, the need-a-pair end (len 1, odd trailing, len truncation), the NUL first-character exit, all three first-character ranges and their below/above neighbours, the same for the second character, the digit/a-f/A-F value conversions for both nibbles, and the written<count loopback taken and not taken (count exact, count at capacity, count past the text). Three edges are declared dead above: the null-text exit and the two value-conversion xor fall-throughs.
allowedImageReads is empty: the function reads only its two buffers, no image constants (its hex ranges are immediates).

acknowledgedGaps.why: The client returns 0 at 0x14269ab98 (`test r8, r8; je 0x14269acaf`). The arena probe always supplies a non-null pointer, so this edge is declared unreachable above; a len of 0 (the sibling guard at 0x14269aba1) is covered and returns the same 0.

acknowledgedGaps.what: a count larger than the out buffer, or a len larger than the text buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client writes count bytes and reads len characters with no bounds checks; either overrun is a caller bug that would write/read past the arena. The probe rejects both and the fixture never builds one (count <= 32 = OUT_LEN, len <= len(text) <= 64).

The client does not check rcx at all: with a non-zero count and a valid pair it would write to address 0 and fault. The arena probe always supplies a non-null out buffer, so this caller bug is not a tested path and the shipped helper, like the client, has no null check.
